problem_statement:
feat(sandbox): add opt-in 'sandbox' mode -- disposable container per run

A fifth HARNESS_SAFETY mode alongside auto/approve/dryrun/plan, picked
explicitly per run (/mode sandbox or HARNESS_SAFETY=sandbox). Every
other mode is completely unaffected -- day-to-day use never launches
a container, matching how Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode work directly on
the host today.

In sandbox mode, run_command executes inside a disposable, per-
workspace container (one launched lazily on first use, reused for the
session, --rm on stop) instead of directly on the machine. File reads/
writes/edits are untouched in every mode: the workspace is bind-
mounted into the container, so both sides see identical bytes, and
Wells' own path confinement already keeps writes inside WORKSPACE_ROOT
regardless of mode -- only arbitrary shell execution needed isolating.

Runtime-agnostic by design, not Docker-only: every call is a plain OCI
run/exec/stop, auto-detecting Podman first (daemonless on Linux,
lighter VM on Mac/Windows, no Docker Desktop licensing concerns) and
falling back to Docker. WELLS_SANDBOX_RUNTIME pins the choice.

Verified live end-to-end against a real Docker daemon: container
launch, bind-mount visibility, OS-level isolation (Linux container vs
Windows host), container reuse across calls, and clean teardown all
confirmed. codeact.py's run_code is not yet routed through the
sandbox -- noted as a follow-up in sandbox.py's module docstring.

Docs: new Safety model row + WELLS_SANDBOX_IMAGE/WELLS_SANDBOX_RUNTIME
config entries, /mode help text, sandbox.py in the project structure list.
